messages:
maria: quick check — i'm thinking about adding a lightweight GC pass that coalesces tiny free ranges in host staging to fight long tail fragmentation. thoughts?
jamal: curious — is this a synchronous compaction or opportunistic background?
maria: opportunistic. idea is: when host staging idle cycles detected, run a scan that merges adjacent free spans and drops tiny islands under a threshold. should be bounded work.
andrew: what triggers 'idle cycles'? can we avoid interfering with prefetch/async warmup?
maria: heuristic: cpu load < 30% on the host pool + no inflight microbatches for 200ms. it's a soft signal — cancel if we see incoming warmup.
sre-jen: watch out for bursty traffic patterns. a background compaction could increase page faults if it races with prefetch, causing extra transfers. need ramp-down/backoff.
jamal: also: merging ranges might move metadata around. allocator API change? do we need to pin/unpin during compaction?
katie: allocator should expose a stable handle. we can add a 'try_compact(span_handle, flags)' that returns remap info if it moves. users that keep direct device pointers must opt-in.
andrew: or we keep compaction within host staging only — never touch resident GPU backing. that avoids invalidating device pointers but still reduces fragmentation in host pools.
maria: exactly — plan A: host-only compaction. Plan B: if coordinator decides to promote a span to resident and it's fragmented, do an aligned copy with short stall and update KV cache.
jamal: what about GC and prefetch interaction? Pre-fetcher might be pulling prefixes into host staging while GC is merging. We need ordering guarantees to avoid double-copy.
katie: simple approach: prefetcher annotates spans with 'prefetch-inflight' tag. compactor skips tagged spans. compactor can remove tag when done. lightweight and avoids stalls.
sre-jen: metrics we need: compaction time, avoided allocations per hour, extra page transfers triggered, and worst-case stall duration. Let's add SLI for compaction-induced faults.
andrew: one more tradeoff: small-span coalescing reduces external fragmentation but increases chance of large contiguous allocations being held by a single tenant — affects fairness. we should respect tenant soft-quotas.
maria: good point — compactor will respect tenant affinity and not coalesce across tenant boundaries unless both tenants under-utilized.
jamal: eviction interplay: if compaction runs and frees host pages, eviction logic should see those pages as reclaimable immediately, not treat them as recently used. update residency timestamps on compaction.
katie: implementation sketch: 1) scanner thread picks candidate spans by size/window 2) obtain lightweight lease from allocator 3) if lease granted, migrate live subobjects to a new span (memcpy) 4) update mappings via atomic swap 5) release old span to free list. all async.
andrew: ensure atomic swap is epoched with in-flight inference. use the existing request-quiesce token or a minimal RCU.
maria: small PoC plan for next week: integrate host compactor into staging pool, opt-in flag, expose metrics, and run on a couple of canary hosts. if we see any 99.9th latency blips, kill and iterate.
sre-jen: :thumbsup: add feature flag and tempo rollout. I'll add a runbook step to disable via console and patch drain.
runtime-bot: deploy-preview: host-compactor-poc created for canary-group-3 at revision rfc/host-compactor-2026.
maria: thanks — i'll drop a short PR and basic perf numbers once PoC runs.
jamal: also record a note for future: consider cross-pool compaction (hot-slot shuffle) if we later add NUMA-aware pools — but that's v2.
katie: ack, adding to next-quarters backlog.
andrew: cool. i'm out for now — ping if you want help validating atomic swap semantics.
maria: thanks all. will follow up with results.
